rationale.conceptual: Non-trivial application of well-known methods (DFT-GGA, quasi-harmonic Debye model, shell-model MD) with careful parameter choices and proper extraction of bulk modulus and thermal expansivity from EV data, requiring thermodynamic knowledge but no novel algorithms.
rationale.execution: Pipeline with about 5 stages: DFT energy-volume calculation, QHD post-processing, two independent MD simulations (SM and BSM) each over a grid of conditions, and final CSV compilation. Each stage uses a different code (Quantum ESPRESSO, Gibbs2, LAMMPS) requiring installation and appropriate input/output handling.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper applies established computational methods (DFT+QHD, shell-model MD) to MgO. The conceptual challenge is correctly implementing these methods and extracting thermodynamic properties. Execution involves a multi-step pipeline using three separate codes and combining results.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT on a small unit cell (2 atoms) and MD on 1000 atoms at moderate cutoffs; all CPU-based and lightweight, with negligible data volume.
